name: Context Menu
summary: Context-triggered menu that reuses Dropdown Menu item anatomy while adding fixed positioning, contextmenu entry points, keyboard invocation, and dismissal behavior.

anatomy.name: root
anatomy.description: Fixed-position menu surface anchored to a context interaction point.

anatomy.name: item
anatomy.description: Inherited Dropdown Menu item used for context commands.

anatomy.name: separator
anatomy.description: Inherited separator used to group context commands.

sizes.name: default
sizes.description: Default context menu width and item spacing.

states.name: open
states.description: Visible state controlled by the context-menu--open modifier.

behavior.name: visibility
behavior.description: The context menu is hidden by default and becomes visible when context-menu--open is applied.

behavior.name: entryPoints
behavior.description: The menu should open from pointer contextmenu events and keyboard context menu entry points.

behavior.name: positioning
behavior.description: The menu should position near the invocation point while clamping inside the viewport.

behavior.name: menuSemantics
behavior.description: The inherited menu items must preserve menu semantics and disabled behavior.

behavior.name: dismissal
behavior.description: The menu should close on Escape, outside interaction, viewport changes, or completed commands.

properties.name: open
properties.description: Controls whether the context menu surface is visible; invocation coordinates and viewport clamping remain target behavior.

accessibility: Provide keyboard access through Shift+F10 or the Menu key when a context menu is available.
Do not make critical actions available only through a context menu.
Use the Dropdown Menu item semantics and disabled behavior for inherited menu items.
Move focus into the menu while it is open and restore focus to the invoking element when it closes.
Close on Escape and outside interaction.

web.notes: Implemented by class composition in components/css/layout.css and inherited Dropdown Menu classes; invocation and positioning behavior must be provided by the consuming target.
